strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Raising ratemaking sophistication for large commercial accounts while large-account competition slows growth
posting_evidence: Senior Analyst, Actuarial Pricing for Commercial & Specialty Lines, Montréal, hybrid; base 87,200–106,600 plus 10% bonus target; no posting date stated (reposted roughly 2 months ago per Built In).
Mandate: support strategic initiatives to improve ratemaking sophistication and help explain nationwide performance, including earnings-call preparation.
Scope: actuarial support for large-account pricing across 22+ lines of business, covering indications, rate committees and corporate planning.
Tools and profile: Python, VBA, R or SAS; 3+ years of P&C actuarial experience, ACAS preferred; guides and coaches team members.
Must be eligible to work in Canada; Intact states it does not sponsor work permits.

news.summary: Intact's Q2 2026 Canadian commercial lines posted an 85.7% combined ratio on 1% operating DPW growth, with competition in large commercial accounts tempering growth initiatives; the 12-month outlook for commercial and specialty lines stayed at low to mid-single-digit premium growth.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Inference: with commercial lines very profitable (85.7% combined ratio) but growing only 1% amid large-account competition, Intact likely wants more granular large-account rating so it can compete selectively without giving up margin. The posting's link to rate committees and earnings-call preparation suggests this pricing team feeds executive views of performance, not just technical rate filings. For the candidate this is a technical actuarial pricing role, not a commercial pricing-strategy role; it fits only with an actuarial background.
open_questions: How much of the large-account work is underwriter-led, account-by-account pricing versus rate-plan indications?
Is the requisition still open, or has it been filled and reposted? The employer page could not be found.
What modelling stack (GLM or ML) and governance does the CL&SL pricing team use for its 22+ lines of business?
strategy_updates.caveat: Based on a job-board copy of the posting (Talent.com/Built In), not the employer's own page, plus one earnings-coverage article; no current-rate figures were found.
